There are two series I am a fan of;<u> The Wheel of Time</u> & <u>The Chronicals of Thomas Covenant</u>, from here on out Chronicals of Thomas Covenant will be referred to as "CTC"

Both feature a creator who has imprisoned an enemy: In CTC the Creator crafted the metaphysical foundation of reality called The Arch of Time, and crafted the world within in. His antithesis, Lord Foul, corrupted the work during the crafting. When the Creator discovered this, he contested with Lord Foul and, victorious, imprisoned him within the Arch. Lord Fouls' ultimate goal is to destroy the Arch and claim all of reality. The main difference between CTC and WoT is Lord Foul is a physical presence in the world, though at times he is dispersed and weakened. In both series the Creator cannot or will not actively intervene in the war against his antithesis. We dont know why the Creator in WoT refuses to act but CTCs' wont because doing so would break the Arch and release Lord Foul. I can think of 2 reasons why WoTs' Creator wont; either he doesn't care, or intevening will destroy the Wheel and achieve Shai'tans objective anyway.

Both series feature a prophesied magic-wielding saviour. in CTC it is a man called Thomas Covenant, a leper from our world (the "real" world) who is summoned into The Land by magic. He wears a white gold wedding ring as a reminder of his lost wife (who divorced him after his diagnosis, ostensibly to protect their infant son). In The Land, his ring is "...the wild magic that destroys peace..." & Thomas is prophesied to "...save or damn..."
